headline: Agentic QA, LLM review workflows, and infra stability: what QA leads must act on today

top_signal.title: JetBrains Research: Framework for Reviewing AI‑Generated Code (trust‑calibration first)
top_signal.summary: JetBrains Research proposes a three‑level review workflow (overview → file risk stratification → snippet checks) and a trust‑calibration focus for reviewing large AI‑generated change sets, backed by participatory study and a conference paper.
top_signal.why_it_matters: QA leads must rework review and test acceptance processes for agent‑written code and tests, prioritizing segment‑level risk signals and tooling that surfaces model confidence.

items.title: Sentry adds Unreal MCP integration so coding agents can set up crash reporting and triage issues
items.category: Agentic QA / Game & native crash triage
items.summary: Sentry’s plugin exposes Sentry tools to Unreal Engine 5.8’s experimental MCP server, letting coding agents configure DSNs, upload symbols, reproduce crashes, and fetch enriched issue context for root‑cause work.
items.why_it_matters: Game and native QA teams can delegate repetitive instrumentation and root‑cause triage to agents while preserving evidence and traceability, accelerating crash‑to‑fix workflows for packaged builds.

items.title: Kotlin Toolchain 0.13 adds agent‑friendly features, smoother iOS/Android onboarding and compiler caches
items.summary: JetBrains released Kotlin Toolchain 0.13: a unified CLI with Hot Reload MCP server, agent skills, iOS simulator auto‑provisioning, improved Android SDK provisioning, and Kotlin/Native per‑file caches to speed native rebuilds and tests.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile QA automation teams should update environment provisioning and test workflows—agentic test generation/maintenance will be more reliable and device/simulator provisioning becomes less brittle.

items.title: Kubernetes: shift to cgroup v2 — resource semantics and compatibility guidance
items.summary: Kubernetes published guidance on moving clusters to cgroup v2, detailing kernel requirements, task freezer behavior, CPU/memory accounting differences, and migration caveats that affect scheduling and observability.
items.why_it_matters: Teams running containerized test runners, load tests or agent sandboxes must validate test harness behavior and performance baselines under cgroup v2 to avoid misleading test regressions.

items.title: NVIDIA publishes AICR v1.0: stable, verifiable GPU cluster configuration
items.summary: NVIDIA’s AICR v1.0 standardizes GPU cluster compatibility (CLI, REST API, SDK, bundle layout, artifact schemas) and declares stable public interfaces to support verifiable, reproducible cluster setups.
items.why_it_matters: ML/LLM test and benchmark teams gain a practical spec to lock down GPU environment variants, improving reproducibility for performance regressions, automated model tests, and CI GPU validation suites.

watch.title: GitHub: fix rolling out to restore agent activity in Copilot usage metrics
watch.summary: GitHub rolled an IDE update to correct under‑reported agent activity in Copilot usage metrics; the fix restores accurate agent lines and activity reporting in usage dashboards.
watch.why_it_matters: QA leads tracking adoption of agentic test generation or review should treat historical Copilot agent metrics as partially undercounted until this fix is applied and compare baselines accordingly.

learning.title: How to evaluate LLMs and agents: benchmarks, application evaluation, and guardrails (LangChain guide)
learning.summary: LangChain’s evaluation guide separates benchmark‑level and application‑level testing, and outlines designing representative tests, scoring strategies, and guardrails for agents and LLMs in production contexts.
learning.why_it_matters: Use this guide to design repeatable, task‑focused LLM/agent evals, lock protocols for CI tests, and choose metrics that expose uncertainty and real‑world failure modes.
